newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-APN says confident of improved 97.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-APN says confident of improved 97.

text.p: Publishing group Australian Provincial Newspapers Ltd said on Wednesday it was confident of improving its earnings in 1997.

"Trading for the first two months of the current year is encouraging, reflecting APN's world class core business of publishing, broadcasting and outdoor advertising," the company said in a statement accompanying 1996 results.
"We are confident of improving APN's earnings in 1997."
Net profit for 1996 was A$26.54 million compared with A$26.39 million a year earlier.
"The group's result is satisfactory and has been achieved in continued difficult trading conditions in many of our markets," chairman Liam Healy said in a statement.

"The company's recent investment in outdoor and transit advertising has been more than vindicated with this division significantly outperforming the forecasts provided to shareholders at the time of acquisition," Healy said.
He said that despite more difficult trading conditions in Queensland throughout much of 1996, regional newspaper earnings before interest and tax was within five percent of 1995 levels.
"This division continued to be affected by depressed local and classified advertising volumes due to the weak overall economy," Healy said.
"However, overall revenues were assisted by increases in national advertising and strong yield gains to counteract thse market driven volume losses," he said.

"The rains have been good in our region, but there has been little pickup yet in spending, because of high levels of rural debt, depressed property/building sectors and low cattle and sugar prices," he added.
Healy said APN had continued its major investment in pre-press technology during the year.
He said installations were now substantially completed and the group was beginning to benefit from reduced operating costs with a significant improvement in productivity.
The group had also benefitted from reduced newsprint costs.

However, Healy said the specialist publishing division had a disappointing year. "This was due to a combination of difficult market conditions, with business to business advertising down by more than 10 percent, but also due to a number of management issues which have been addressed," Healy said.
Overall, the division made a loss in 1996.
"Despite the 1996 result, APN remains committed to specialty publishing," he said.
APN said broadcasting again produced good results, contributing A$14.1 million before abnormals to equity consolidated earnings before interest and tax.
